analysis.title: Korea is sending a warning
key_insights: KOSPI is losing momentum and has slipped below its major trend line. It is well below the 100-day MA while the 200-day MA remains intact for now.
KOSPI has opened a sizable short-term divergence versus the SOX, while investors have recently loaded up on SOX exposure and US semis positioning is increasingly crowded.
Buybacks in KOSPI are going into hibernation, removing an important bid.
KOSPI is still dealing with the hangover from the extreme vol environment during the upside mania. Vol has declined alongside the index falling over the past few sessions.
At the height of the mania KOSPI vol was pricing daily moves of around 6%. That has fallen to just above 2%.
Offloading of calls pressures deltas, and theta remains rich.

KOSPI continues to track inverted crude closely while SPX and NDX have moved beyond the oil narrative. Korea imports virtually all its crude, and oil is more than a third of its primary energy consumption.

Goldman frames the move as a positioning flush, not a structural peak. It cites firm forward estimates, a robust semi/memory cycle (HBM4 ramp, equipment shortages through 2H28) and multi-decade-low valuations, and recommends selectively accumulating high-conviction memory and tech names on dips.
